Commentary.Commentary: The hosts, on the other hand, will want to replicate what they did with the ball in their last innings. Will the home side blow away the Asian side or will the Lankan Lions come roaring back? We will have to wait to find that out.

There is still a lot of time in the game to go but with the wicket crumbling, the visitors' batters will have to pull out a miracle if they are going to win this or even draw the same. A lot will depend on their top order which failed in the first innings.
For Sri Lanka it was once again Lahiru Kumara who stood out. He finished with a three-fer. He was well supported by Herath who got two to his name. However, their batters now face an uphill task.

Jason Holder calls his batters back which means, WINDIES HAVE DECLARED for the second time in this Test! Three overs is all they played after the break. Added 14 in the 18 balls they faced and have given Sri Lanka a target of 453. They started their second innings with a lead of 229. Their batsmen came out with a positive approach yesterday but kept losing wickets at regular intervals. Kieran Powell was their star man but he missed out on a deserving ton. Holder too played a quickfire knock this morning to ensure the hosts have a total which one would reckon is enough on this wicket.
Full on middle, hit down to long on for a run.
Fires this outside off, Bishoo guides it through point for a run.
Slogs it against the turn for the deep square leg fielder for a run. The lead is now 450.
Very full outside off, Roach slaps it to covers. He is disappointed as he could not hit it past that fielder.
Fires it full on off, Bishoo tries to drive but gets an inside edge towards fine leg for a run.
Goes after him straightaway but gets only a run. On the pads, Roach slogs it uppishly towards deep square leg for a run.
Rangana Herath comes into the attack.
This time goes short and outside off, Bishoo tries to reach out for it with a cut shot but does not connect.
A yorker on leg stump. Roach tries to jam it out but it goes off the bottom edge down to fine leg for a run.
The slower ball down the leg side. The batsman walks across and tries to clip but he seems to have missed it.

Just misses the stumps! A fullish delivery from the bowler on middle and off, hits the seam and it jumps sharply. Roach goes for the lofted drive but fails to make contact and the ball goes over the stumps.
Widish delivery from the pacer and Bishoo slaps it to deep point. He rotates the strike with a single.
Width on offer from Lakmal, Bishoo flashes hard but fails to put bat to ball.
Suranga Lakmal comes into the attack.
Flatter ball outside off, Roach splices it away to deep point for a brace. So seven runs from the opening over of the second session. We can safely say there is some intent.
Delivers it full on the pads, Roach goes for the big shot but gets it off the inner half to fine leg for a brace.
Sliding away from the stumps, Roach goes hard at it. The ball catches the outer half and flies to third man. A couple more added to the total.
Perera serves up a full delivery, Bishoo makes room and powers it to the right of Mathews at mid off. They take a quick single.
Flatter ball from Perera, angling in from outside off. Bishoo looks to sweep that but fails to make contact and gets hit on the front pad.
Tossed up delivery on the stumps,  the batsman defends it back to the bowler.

So no declaration in the break. How many more runs will they be looking to add? Get to the 450-run mark? Maybe. They need another 12 runs for that as Devendra Bishoo and Kemar Roach make their way out to the middle. Dilruwan Perera to bowl.
...Day 4, Session 2...

Holder then came out and started to play his shots right from the beginning. He along with Powell built a 42-run stand before the southpaw fell 12 short of a ton. He was soon followed by Holder who was Rangana Herath's second scalp. Bishoo and Roach then joined hands to play out the remaining overs before Lunch. The lead is quite a big one now and it will be interesting to see if the Windies come out to bat after the break. Even if they do, what kind of approach will they get with them? Join us for the second session to find out.

We witnessed an interesting session. One would have expected the Windies to come out and score at a brisk rate but that has not been the case. They have only managed to score 78 runs in the 29 overs bowled, taking their lead up to 438. Powell did start the day with intent but Dowrich was the complete opposite. He was happy to play the blocking game but eventually fell prey to Kumara to a ball which stayed a touch low.
The last ball before the break is slow and tossed up outside off. The batter lets it be. LUNCH ON DAY 4!
Flighted ball on off, Roach continues doing what he has done till now. DEFEND.
Bowls it with a round-arm action and on the middle stump. Roach covers the line of the delivery and plays to the short leg fielder.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
On the stumps, defended.
Flighted ball on off, Roach comes forward and keeps it out.
Back of a length on off, Roach pushes it through covers for a run.
On a length around off, defended.
A good delivery! Length around off, this one shapes away after pitching. Roach first thinks of playing at it but then pulls his bat out of the way.
Shorter in length outside off, Bishoo evades it.
Bowls it short again outside off, Gamage has bowled one bad ball in each of his last few overs. Bishoo cuts it through backward point. There is a man in the deep and a single results.
Fullish on middle, Bishoo mistimes it to the man at mid on.
Flatter by Herath on middle, the batter works it to mid-wicket. A maiden for Herath.
Another tossed up delivery on middle, Roach is happy to block it out.
Gives it air on leg stump. Kemar comes onto the front foot and keeps it out.
Floats it up on middle, Kemar defends it.
Loopy ball on the leg stump. Roach prods forward and blocks it.
Flighted ball on middle, Roach lunges forward and keeps it out.
Hits the length again on middle, Bishoo pushes it back to mid on.
Gamage bowls it fuller on off, Bishoo pushes it to the man at covers.
FOUR! Poor ball and put away! An easy one for Bishoo as this is down the leg side. All he had to do was to put bat on it. He does so and it races away fine on the leg side.
Back of a length on off, Bishoo pushes it to mid off.
Attacks the stumps, offers no room to the batsman. He keeps it out.

Ian Bishop makes a point about declaring before the break. He observes that now-a-days, captains do not prefer declaring before a break. Reason being, the break gives enough time for the fielding side to change its gear and come out fresh. So ideally, do not declare before Lunch, come out, play 2 overs and then declare. That might set the cat free amongst the pigeons. Guess Jason Holder and Stuart Law might be thinking the same...
Short and wide outside off, Bishoo misses the cut shot. Once again a ball which he could have scored on goes abegging.
Flighted ball on the stumps, Roach, just like Bishoo defends it out.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Loopy ball on middle, Kemar lunges and keeps it out.
Floats it up on off, Roach defends it onto the ground.
Flatter and on leg stump. Roach tries to keep it out but is hit on the pads.
Kemar Roach is the next man in.

OUT! No inside edge and Holder is a dead duck! He was looking to score right from the word go and falls playing an innovative shot. He brings out the reverse sweep but picks the wrong ball. It is very full and around middle and leg. He fails to get his bat down in time and the ball hits his pads. The players appeal and the umpire after giving it a thought raises his finger. Holder challenges the decision as he signals the 'T'. Time for the replays and they first check for the inside edge. Snicko confirms there is no bat involved. Hawk Eye then shows three reds. Holder is given his marching orders but Bishoo stays out there which means the Windies will carry onto bat. However, an enterprising innings by the Windies skipper comes to an end.
Review time! Holder has been given LBW. He wants to take it upstairs. It looks to be quite adjacent, only an inside edge can save him there.
The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball.
Short and wide outside off, Bishoo goes for the cut but misses.
Back of a length on off, DB defends it to point.

FOUR! This is very useful! Hopefully for the Windies this should get Bishoo going now. This is short and outside off, Bishoo slashes at it. The ball goes off the outside edge down to the third man fence for a boundary.
Fuller and on middle, Holder eases it down to long on. They have the field back to the Windies skipper. They do not mind him taking the singles.
Goes shorter and outside off, Holder takes a few steps ahead and lets it go to the keeper.
Make that 12 balls now. A maiden from Herath as he darts this on off. Bishoo blocks it. He is on 3 from 25. Not sure about the intent he has come out with.
Just a single in the last 11 balls faced by Bishoo. He pushes this towards mid-wicket.
Floats it up on off, Bishoo strokes it back to the bowler.
Fires this one on off, Bishoo is happy to keep it out.
Works it with the turn to the man at mid-wicket.
Flatter on off, Bishoo lunges and blocks it out.
A single off the last ball! I don't think Sri Lanka will have a problem with that. This is short and outside off, Bishoo guides it through point and gets to the other end. Just one from the over.
5 dots in a row by Gamage! Back of a length on off, Bishoo pushes it to covers.
Another forward defensive shot by Bishoo.
Fuller and outside off, a ball which could have been hit for runs. Bishoo drives it to covers.
Goes fuller again, Bishoo is happy to push it to the man at covers. He looks in no hurry here. He is now looking to get himself in.
On a good length around off, Bishoo defends it to the man at point.
Works it around the corner with the turn for a run.
Holder swings but does not get it off the middle. It goes off the inner half towards deep square leg for a run.
Bishoo gets off the mark, ON HIS 12th BALL! He eases this down to long on and gets to the other end.
Uses his feet and gets to the pitch of it. Holder drives it to the man at long off for a run.
Plays the reverse sweep but finds the fielder at point.
The batsman has driven it through mid on.
Another dot! Not sure of the idea of trying to block the balls. Bishoo defends this one onto the ground.
Fuller in length on off, Bishoo drives it to the man at mid off.
Length outside off, Bishoo tries to keep it out off the back foot but is beaten by the low bounce.
Good length on off, Bishoo defends it on the back foot.
Back of a length on off, Holder punches it through covers for a run.
Goes fuller on middle, Holder hits it down to long on.
Lahiru Gamage is back on.
Finds the edge but it is well short of the slip fielder! Loopy ball on off, Bishoo goes back on the back foot and tries to defend but gets an outside edge which goes wide of first slip.
Floats it up on off, Bishoo off the front foot keeps it out.
Nicely bowled! He bowls the arm ball on off, Bishoo lunges and tries to defend. He plays for the non-existent turn and gets beaten.
Eases this down to long off for a run.
Floats it up on off, Holder keeps it out off the front foot.
Rangana Herath who is now into the attack, flights this up on off. Holder defends it onto the ground.
Quicker on off, Bishoo defends off the back foot.
Flatter on off, Bishoo defends it off the back foot.
Flatter on off, Bishoo guides it to the man at point.
Flatter on middle, Bishoo defends it on the front foot.
Devendra Bishoo walks out to the middle.

OUT! CAUGHT! No ton for Powell! He falls to the leg stump line trap. Powell uses his feet to a ball which is bowled on his pads. He chips it towards mid-wicket where the substitute, Jeffrey Vandersay, takes a good catch diving forward. A dejected Powell starts walking back but he has been asked to wait by the umpires as they want to check for the no ball. Replays roll in and the front foot is fine. Kieran has to continue walking. A good innings by him comes to an end in a very soft manner. He will be disappointed of missing out on a ton but on a larger context, Windies now need to get a move on.
The keeper now is standing outside the leg stump and Dilruwan bowls it there. Powell goes for the paddle sweep but finds the fielder at short fine leg.

FOUR! TOP SHOT! Fuller and on off, Holder plays it with a straight bat towards the bowler. He tries to stop it with his feet which is never a good idea. He fails to do so and the ball races to the long off fence. The lead is now 20 more than 400.
Goes very full on middle, Powell wrists it down to mid on and sets off for a run. The fielder has a shy at the bowler's end but misses.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot. The batsmen have run through for a single.
BEATEN! Length around off, this one straightens after pitching. Holder has a feel for it but gets beaten.
Good length on off, defended.
Good length on off, kept out towards covers for a run.
Powell uses his feet but a touch too early. Dilruwan sees that and shortens his length. Powell tucks it around the corner and works it through square leg for a run.
Changes the angle and goes around the wicket. He angles it on off, Holder tries to play across the line but the ball takes the leading edge and goes towards point for a single.
FOUR! Swept and swept fine! 10 runs from the over so far. Holder goes down on one knee and sweeps it through square leg. The fielder in the deep does dive to stop it but his effort goes in vain.
Flatter and on off, Holder defends it off the back foot.
Floats it up on middle, Holder works it to the man at mid-wicket.
SIX! That shot might have just indicated that the declaration is not far away! Dilruwan tosses it up on off, Holder goes for the heave, connects well and it clears the long on fence.

Drinks break. It has been a dull first hour so far, the Windies overnight pair played quite sedately but credit must be given to the Sri Lankan bowlers. They kept things tight and didn't bowl many freebies.
Fuller length ball on off, the batsman plays a drive on the off side. A maiden over from Lahiru Gamage to end the first hour of play.
Fullish delivery on off, Powell plays a drive to mid off. Once again he fails to find the gap.
Length ball from Gamage, the batsman sits back and punches it to the cover region.
Gamage serves a full delivery on the stumps, Powell defends it back to the bowler.
Angles it in from outside off and Powell pushes it to covers.
Just short of gully! On a length outside off, Powell goes on the back foot to cut that but the ball goes off the outer half to gully. It lands just short of the fielder.
Lahiru Gamage comes into the attack.
Faster one on the middle and leg stump line, Holder pushes it to mid on.

FOUR! Execution was spot on! With that boundary, the Windies lead has crossed the 400-run mark! Loopy delivery outside off from Perera and Holder plays a reverse sweep to perfection. He clears the man at short third man and picks up a boundary. How many more will the Windies want before they declare now?
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Appeal for an LBW but the umpire isn't impressed! Loopy ball on off from Perera, Holder goes for the reverse sweep but gets an inside edge on the pads.
Flatter ball from Perera. It spins a little and Holder pushes it back to the bowler.
Tossed up delivery outside off, the batsman lunges on the front foot and defends it.
Dilruwan Perera is into the attack for the first time today.
Goes fuller this time on middle, it is eased to the man at mid on.

The left-hander cops another blow! He this time though has a helmet on to protect him. This is short and at a good pace on the body of the batsman. He goes for the pull but the ball hits his gloves and goes onto hit the grille.
Holder gets another run as he works it around the corner.
Down the leg side, Powell works it down to fine leg and takes a run. He is now 15 short of a ton.
Back of a length on off, Powell defends it onto the ground off the back foot.
Angles it on the pads, Holder works it to the man at fine leg and gets to the other end,
The batsman dances down the track but decides to defend it.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
The batsman plays the Square-Cut. Good running between the wickets to pick up three runs.
Powell uses his feet and gets to the pitch of the delivery. Powers it to long on and rotates the strike.
Fires it flat on the stump, Holder taps it to mid-wicket and gets across with a single.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.

OUCH, OUCH! That must be painful! Short, doesn't come as a surprise to the viewers. Kumara has been troubling the pair with that length. He attacks the body and Powell hops back to fend that but he misses. The ball smashes into his rib cage. The batsman isn't wearing a chest guard which is pretty surprising.

No, no, no! That is not the shot you want to be playing against this man. Bangs it in short and down the leg side. Powell goes for the pull but misses it. That could have easily brushed his glove and given Sri Lank another wicket.
Holder tucks a delivery from Kumara on the leg side and gets down to other end with a single.
BOUNCER! It is another well-directed one from the pacer. On this occasion, Holder is smart enough to duck under and not attempt a shot.
Powell drops a delivery on his pads on to the leg side and they take a single.
Short ball and it nearly does the trick for Kumara! Holder is rushed by that one as he attempts a pull. Miscues it wide of the fielder at leg gully. Single taken.
Floated delivery on off, Powell goes across and defends it back towards the bowler.
Eases it through the covers for another single and lead moves to 386 for the hosts.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.

FOUR! Big shot from Holder, seems like he has come out with an intent to give this innings some spark. Loopy ball from Herath, the batsman gets on the front foot and lofts it away to long off for a one bounce boundary.
Flatter from Herath and the batsman slices it towards short third man for a single.
Floated delivery on off, Powell lunges on the front foot and defends it out.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the backfoot.
Powell goes across and taps it to the left of the mid on fielder for a single.
Holder gets on the front foot and defends it to the cover region for a quick single. He is off the mark straightaway.
Jason Holder, the Windies skipper, strides out to bat.

OUT! PLUMB! At least that is what it looked to me. Lahiru Kumara is once again the man for Sri Lanka. He has been phenomenal with the ball in this game for the visitors and once again he provides them with a breakthrough. Shane Dowrich, the star batsman for the Windies in the first innings, departs without making much of an impact. It is a pacey delivery from the fast bowler, pitches on a length, angles in sharply and not to forget, it keeps low too. Dowrich makes the mistake of hanging on the back foot to a delivery which he should have played off the front foot. The ball pings him below the knee roll and the fielders go up in a flash. The umpire raises his finger and on seeing that the two West Indian players have a chat and decide not to challenge the decision. The ball tracking confirms it was a good call from the two as the ball would have crashed on to the leg stump. It was a strange innings from the wicket-keeper batsman considering the fact that his side is well ahead in the game.
Short of a length ball on off, Dowrich sits back and defends it to the cover region. It goes straight to the fielder and that's a dot.
Kumara starts a new over with a delivery on the pads and Powell flicks it in front of square leg for a run. The southpaw moves to 80.
Herath bowls a delivery on the stumps, it skids a little but Dowrich manages to tap it to short leg.
Dorwich dances down the track and powers it to mid on. But he finds the fielder.
Faster one from Herath on the stumps and the batsman defends it out.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Loopy ball and Powell works it with the spin towards mid-wicket for a single. Lead for the Windies is now 377.
Faster one on the stumps from Herath, Powell gets right back and defends it out.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Dowrich pushes a delivery from Kumara on the off side.
Short of a length ball, Powell pushes it through the cover region for a single.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.

Fuller length ball from Kumara, Powell punches it down the track. There is a fielder for such shots at silly mid off. Chandimal there, moves across in an attempt to stop it but collides with Dowrich who holds his ground. The ball rolls down towards the long off fence, Herath gives it a chase from mid on and pulls it inside the ropes. Two more added to the total. Chandimal was not happy but the non-striker was not at fault there.

Was that a chance? Nope. It landed well short of Roshen. Kumara nearly makes an impact straightaway. He bowls it short and the batsman pulls it in front of square leg. The fielder from the deep charges in and puts in a full length dive. The ball just lands short of him but Silva does really well to stop that one. 100 on 100 for the fielding effort.
Lahiru Kumara, the most successful bowler for Sri Lanka in this game, comes into the attack.
Positive footwork from Powell, he sees the loopy delivery and steps out. Forces it to long on for a single.
Slightly straight from Herath, the batsman works it past the man at short leg. Crosses over and gives the strike back to Powell.
Delivers the ball on the middle and leg stump line and we get to see another defensive stroke from the Windies wicket-keeper.
Pushes it much quicker and the batsman taps it to mid-wicket.
Loopy ball, Dowrich drives it to mid off but can't find the gap though.
Uses his wrists and works it with the spin to the left of the mid-wicket fielder. Powell collects another run and the lead ticks over.
Lakmal goes wide of the crease and bowls it on the stumps. The batsman is happy to defend those.
Serves up a good length ball outside off, Dowrich defends it point.
On a length from Lakmal and the southpaw defends it to the vacant cover region. They take a single.
The left-hander stays back and opens the face of the bat as he guides it to backward point.
Bowls it fuller and outside off. Powell covers his stumps and lets it through to the keeper.
Back of a length ball on off, Powell stands tall and punches it through the covers. The Windies pair scampers back for the second run. Good aggressive running!
Another defensive stroke from Dowrich to end the over. Both the Windies batsmen aren't looking for any big shots at the moment, they are happy to spend some time in the middle.
Tossed up delivery on middle, the right-hander drives it to mid off.
Herath bowls it on the leg stump line and the batsman taps it to short leg.
Angles it in from outside off and Dowrich defends it confidently down the track.
Gives it more air on this occasion and the batsman defends it to covers.
Powell uses his feet to get to the pitch of it. He drills it down the ground to long on for a single.
Nice swing for Lakmal, but he once again is guilty of bowling it too wide. Dowrich lets it be.
Lakmal tries a shortish delivery but bowls it wide outside off and the batsman pushes it with ease towards covers.
Just dips in a little after pitching, the southpaw gets his bat down in time and glances it to fine leg for another single.
Good length ball on the off stump line, Powell defends it down the track.
Touch too straight from Lakmal, maybe is trying for the glory ball. It doesn't swing and Dowrich nudges it away to fine leg for a single.

Superb delivery! Unluckily for Lakmal, he doesn't find the outside edge! Shortish delivery on off, rises sharply and straightens a little. Dowrich looks to defend that but plays down the wrong line. The ball whistles past the outside edge.
Pushes it quicker through the air and gets a defensive stroke in response from the batsman.
Arm ball from Herath from around the wicket angle. The southpaw blocks it solidly.
Loopy ball, the batsman steps out a little and blocks it on the leg side.
Powell moves across and works it on the leg side.
Darts this one on the off stump line, the batsman defends it out.

FOUR! Brilliant shot! First runs off the morning for the Windies and Powell! The bowler drops it short outside off, the left-hander rocks on the back foot and slaps it through the covers. No stopping that one.
Rangana Herath will bowl from the other end. He starts with a man at short leg and just a lone slip fielder.
Fullish delivery from Lakmal, Dowrich pushes to mid off. Maiden over to start Day 4.
Attacks the stumps, doesn't give any room to work with. Dowrich works it to mid wicket.
On a length closer to the off stump, the right-hander sits back and dabs it towards cover-point.
Pulls his length back just a little, and seeing that Dowrich stays in the crease. He defends it on the off side.
Bowls another full delivery in search of some swing, but it isn't there. The batsman flicks it to mid on.

Gentle full delivery from Lakmal, it is in line with the stumps. Dowrich pushes it confidently back towards the bowler. Lakmal dives to his right and makes a good stop. Saves a run or two for his side.
Players are taking their positions. Kieran Powell and Shane Dowrich will resume their innings. For Sri Lanka, Suranga Lakmal will kick-start the proceedings on Day 4. We are all set to go..

PITCH REPORT - The legendary Indian opening batsman, Sunil Gavaskar says that one end of the wicket has behaved really well and the batsmen who are looking to spend time can still do good on this wicket. But as he moves towards the other end, he says there are a few cracks and if the bowlers pitch consistently in that area they can cause a lot of trouble.

The weather will play a key role from here on in this game. The home team will not want any of it for the next two days. While the visitors will welcome it with both arms wide open, the fans of the Asian team will be praying for the heavens to open up and take some time out of this game. Forecast though for today is promising for cricket and we keep our fingers crossed that it stays that way. Let the sport take the front seat and entertain all of us...

Hello and welcome to Day 4 of the first Test between West Indies and Sri Lanka in Port of Spain, Trinidad. The Windies have got a hefty lead, which they would like to further extend and bat Sri Lanka out of this game. Whereas, the Asian team will be on the damage control mode and picking early wickets will help them in that. They would then hope to bat well in their second essay and make the hosts sweat hard for their wickets, contrasting of what they did in their first innings. The morning session promises to be an intriguing one. Do stay tuned  for all the action.
... Day 4, Session 1...

Earlier, the hosts choked the opposition with disciplined bowling. Apart from the promising 78-run stand between Chandimal and Dickwella, rest of the batsmen struggled. A downfall resulted which saw the visitors losing 5 for 45 to get bundled out for a paltry score. It was a collective effort from the Windies bowlers. By handing such an advantage, they were always bound to toil hard. To keep things in perspective, the hosts lead by a massive 360 runs and still have batting to come. It will require something spectacular from the Lankans to script a comeback. Join us for Day 4 at 1000 Local (1400 GMT) to catch all the action. Adios!

Kieran Powell displayed just that and mixed caution with aggression to perfection. He played some eye-catchy strokes and found some decent support from Roston Chase. Together, they stitched a 44-run stand to further strengthen their place. The Sri Lankan bowlers bowled their hearts out but they were always under pressure.

The Windies are well and truly in the ascendancy. They have once again performed excellently today to make the pole position their own. However, on a surface which has become quite two-paced and is playing tricks, their top-order batsmen didn't show much patience and departed to some rash strokes. Lahiru Kumara was the star again as he troubled the batsmen with his consistency. You can argue that a lead of 229 runs gave them the comfort zone to go for their strokes but there should be a method to the madness.

Bowls a tossed up delivery outside off, Dowrich comes on the front foot and pushes it to the left of the mid off fielder for a single. That is it for the day gentlemen, says the umpire and flicks the bails with the cap in his hand. It is STUMPS ON DAY 3!

Oh wow! He is challenging both the edges of the bat. Suddenly, this pitch has spiced up. An arm ball from Perera, it slides on after pitching. The right-hander plays slightly inside the line of it and gets it off the outer half. The fielder at first slip manages to block it.
Once again there is some turn for Dilruwan Perera! An off spinner from Perera, turns in a little, Dowrich covers the line of it and blocks.
Pushes it quicker through the air, the batsman drives it to mid on.
Turn and bounce! It kisses the surface and jumps sharply with some turn. Dowrich hangs right back and safely dabs it on the leg side.
Floated delivery from Dilruwan on the stumps, Dowrich pushes it to mid on.
Drifting on middle and leg, Dowrich works it to the square leg region for a single.
Faster one from Herath on the stumps and the batsman defends it compactly.
Tossed up delivery on the off stump line, the batsman gets right behind that one and defends it solidly right under his eyes.
Herath wants few extra men near the batsman. Two fielder come under the lid, one at short leg and the other at silly point.
Loopy delivery, Shane takes a stride ahead and dead-bats it.
Slow through the air on the same channel, kept out watchfully.
Tossed up generously outside off, defended solidly off the front foot.
Spinning in sharply from outside off, Dowrich pushes at it with hard hands but gets a thick outside edge towards backward square leg. A run taken.
Fullish ball on middle, Dowrich eases it towards mid on.
Outside off, Dowrich leans ahead in defense.
FOUR! Poor delivery and duly punished! A half-tracker down the leg side, Dowrich lines it up and pulls it through fine leg to find the fence.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Goes deep in the crease and counters this one nicely.
In the air... but safe! Going down the leg side, Dowrich goes for the sweep but gets a top edge. The ball lobs behind and falls safely in the short fine leg region. A run taken.
Edged but safe! Outside off, doesn't turn this time. Dowrich pushes at it but gets an outside edge well wide of the first slip fielder. A couple taken.
Tight lines from Herath, Dowrich is equal to the task as he covers the line and blocks it.
Hangs deep in the crease and works it nicely towards mid-wicket.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Tossed up around off, defended solidly off the front foot.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot.
Spins in from outside off, the right-hander looks to defend that but gets it off the inner half to mid-wicket for a single. With that run, West Indies lead touches the 350-run mark.
Much fuller from Perera on this occasion and the batsman gets well forward as he defends it on the track.
Pushed to the cover region by the batsman.
Turning down leg, Dowrich looks to flick that but misses it and gets hit on the thigh pad.
Faster one on the leg stump line, the batsman uses his wrists and works to mid-wicket for a single.
The hero of the first innings, Shane Dowrich is the new man in.

OUT! Castled! The wily old fox has delivered like he has done on so many occasions. However, it is the pitch which has proved to be the undoing of Chase. Coming in with the arm, the ball stays low. Roston goes deep in his crease to clip it across but is foxed by the lack of bounce. The ball hits him on the front pad and deflects back onto the stumps. The Windies lead by 348 runs.
Kieran is nimble on his feet and clips it to long on for a run.

A false stroke! Herath needs to keep on troubling the batsmen. Outside off, Powell plays for the non-existent turn and gets an outside edge. The ball goes past the slip fielder and a couple of runs are taken.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot.
Uses his feet but is not quite to the pitch of this one. Flicks it towards short mid-wicket eventually.
Loopy delivery on a shortish length outside off, Powell goes back and plays it with soft hands towards point.
Rangana Herath is back on.
Fast on middle, turned towards short mid-wicket.
Spinning into Roston who keeps it out watchfully.
Fuller this time, patted back to the bowler.
Leans ahead and drives it with the spin to mid on.
Tossed up delivery, Chase lunges forward in defense.
On a shorter length outside off, Chase goes deep in the crease and guides it through short third man for a brace.
There is an issue with the ball and the umpires are passing it through the 8-shaped gauge. Seems to be fine for the moment.
Full ball going down the leg side, Powell misses the whip.
Fullish delivery, tailing in a touch, Chase accounts for it nicely and taps it towards mid on.
Short of a length outside off, defended solidly off the back foot.
FOUR! Cracking shot! Back of a length and width on offer, Chase stands tall and slaps it through backward point to pick up a boundary.
On a length outside off, angling in, Chase shuffles a touch and works it towards mid on.
Fullish delivery around off, Powell leans ahead in an assured manner and eases it towards covers.
Slow through the air outside off, allows ample time to the southpaw to come down the track and knock it towards long off. A run taken.
Darted in on middle and off, Powell hangs back and punches it out.
Good judgement! Floated around off, spinning away. Powell knows where his off stump is and makes a good leave.
Tossed up outside off, sliced through backward point for a run.
Fullish delivery, Powell misreads the length as he steps out of his crease. Ends up yorking himself but manages to jam it out towards mid on.
Coming in with the arm, turned with the angle through mid-wicket for a run.
Very full ball outside off, Powell drives it off the bottom half of his bat towards mid off.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
On a length around the hips, tucked through square leg for a brace.
Back of a length ball, shaping in, punched crisply off the back foot to the cover region.
A touch fuller in length but this one is pretty wide outside off, an easy leave for Powell.
In the channel outside off, left alone.
Fullish ball on off, Roston defends it watchfully.
Flat on off, Chase defends it with his bat and pad close together.
A bit shorter in length, answered with a straight bat.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Misfield! Shorter in length, Powell punches it towards Chandimal at covers who is a bit lazy to react. Concedes a single.
Quicker one on the leg stump, clipped nicely to deep mid-wicket for a brace.
A delivery that can fit in the harmless category. Chase makes another leave as that is too wide to tempt the batsman.
That one jags back sharply from a good length, Chase shuffles across and decides to shoulders arms.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Another widish delivery from Gamage, the right-hander decides to let it be.
Fuller length ball outside off, it moves away a little. The batsman doesn't play at it.
Gamage bowls it on a length outside off, Roston Chase stays back and lets it through to the keeper.

SIX! 5th Test fifty for Kieran Powell! He was confident from the word go and has played a brilliant knock so far. Tossed up outside off, Powell skips down the track and lifts it nonchalantly over long off. He has timed it really well and the ball sails over the fence. Gets a hug from his partner and applause from the scanty crowd. He will be looking to convert this into a big one.
Fast and accurate from Perera. The southpaw hangs back and pushes it to mid on.
On a flatter trajectory, cut away against the spin towards point.
Floated on middle, Kieran uses his feet and blocks it.
Ooh.. turn! Floated outside off, Chase leans ahead to counter it but gets a thick inside edge which goes between his legs towards short fine leg.
Shorter in length, punched off the back foot towards long on for a single.
In the corridor of uncertainty, holding its line. Chase doesn't fiddle with it.

Leg bye! There was sheer optimism from the Sri Lankans. Swinging down the leg side, Powell falls over a bit in his attempt to flick it and is hit on the pads. The ball rolls towards fine leg and Gamage goes up in an appeal, only to be turned down quickly. A run is taken.
Erring in line, down the leg side, Chase helps it down to fine leg for a run.
Fractionally overpitched outside off, a confident stride forward from Roston as he drives it elegantly to the cover region.

That was tantalizingly close to the off stump! Great stuff from the young man. Good length ball outside off, shaping in substantially. Chase tries to cover the line but is completely foxed to get beaten on the inside. Dickwella dives to his left to collect it.
On a length, angling in, tucked with the angle to deep mid-wicket. A single taken.
Double change. Lahiru Gamage comes in for a burst.
Clears his front leg and milks it towards deep mid off for a single.
Similar delivery, the southpaw is once again to the pitch of it to kill it on the turf.
Tossed up delivery on a fullish length, Kieran lunges forward in defense.
Tentative! Coming in with the arm from around the wicket, Powell is caught in the crease and plays it off the inner half towards mid on.
Spinning in nicely, Roston uses the depth of the crease and turns it through mid-wicket to rotate strike.
Starts off with a floated delivery outside off, Chase drives it with hard hands. Perera dives to his left and makes a good stop.
Time for Drinks.

FOUR! Perfect execution of the straight drive! For all the kids out there, that is how you should play down the ground. Pitched up delivery on off, Powell strides ahead and drives it exquisitely through mid on to get the desired result. The balance was spot on and he holds his pose for the cameramen to click him. The southpaw has played some eye-catching strokes and is looking in great touch.
Full length ball delivery attacking the stumps, Powell shuffles a touch and drives it crisply to mid on.
Nicely played. Similar delivery on the same channel, this time Kieran gets behind it and punches it towards Chandimal at extra cover.
The two-paced nature of the track is once again on display. Good length ball  outside off, stays a bit low. The southpaw tries to push it through the line but the ball passes under his bat.
Back of a length ball outside off, Kieran camps back and plays it with an angled blade towards backward point.
On a length, Powell covers the line and defends it stoutly.
Floated generously outside off, Roston comes forward and pushes it nicely to covers.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
On a flatter trajectory, Chase is a bit tentative and dead-bats it.
Fuller in length, played with the angle towards mid on.
Tossed up delivery, defended solidly off the front foot.
Coming in with the arm, Chase lunges forward in defense.
Fullish delivery, shaping in, Powell defends it with his bat and pad close together.

SIX! Streaky but effective! Short delivery in line of the stumps. Powell goes for a pull shot but the ball gets big on him. Hence, a top edge is induced and the ball sails over fine leg. It is going, going and hits the advertising boards on the full. We saw some top edges from the Sri Lankan lower order fly as well.
On a fuller length outside off, pushed to covers off the front foot.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Short of a length ball, Kieran hops and keeps it out.

Miscommunication but no harm done! Back of a length outside off, Powell taps it towards the right of the bowler and takes off. However, there is no run there and he is rightly sent back by his partner.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Tosses it full outside off, the batsman plays a drive to covers but can't find the gap.
Chase sits on the back foot and defends it on the track.
Gives it more air, seeing the new batsman on strike. Chase leans forward and pushes it to covers.
Tossed up delivery from Herath, the batsman leans on the front foot and powers it through the covers for a boundary.
Faster one on the off stump line, the batsman plays slightly inside the line of it and the ball goes off the outer half on the off side.
On a length outside off, played with an open bat face towards point.
Roston Chase comes out to bat.

OUT! Kumara has been absolutely brilliant and he is reaping the dividends as well. The energy has been right up there from the Sri Lankan players and they are finding a way. This is the second time in the game that the pacer has got rid of Shai Hope. He goes wider of the crease and bowls an effort ball well outside off. It takes off after pitching. Hope goes for a tame push through the line but there is no control whatsoever. Ends up getting a fat outside edge behind. Kusal Mendis at second slip is sharp as a hawk. He leaps to his right and takes a very smart catch and then tumbles down. It has been a really good passage of play for the tourists and they need to keep the pressure on.

Ian Bishop makes a good point on air. He mentions that in the first innings, Powell's head position was not proper and he had paid for the price for that. This time, he showed proper technique to counter the fuller length delivery and got the desired result as well.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads. They pick up a single.
Good response from the bowler! He hits the deck hard and gets the ball to climb on Powell. He gets into an  awkward position but manages to keep it out.

FOUR! Back-to-back boundaries! Steady head, high elbow, and foot towards the pitch of the ball - perfection. Fuller length ball on off, Powell drives it down the ground and the ball whistles away to the long off fence. The lead for the Windies crosses the 300-run mark.
After that boundary, deep point is immediately in place.
FOUR! Powell is oozing confidence at the moment! Kumara angles this one across the southpaw and there is room on offer. Kieran shuffles a touch and smacks it through covers for a rocketing boundary.
Herath sees Powell using his feet and bowls it on a flatter trajectory. The batsman drives it towards wide mid on for a run.
This time he is not assured at all. Spinning in sharply, Kieran is squared up in his stance but manages to defend it off the outer half of his bat.
FOUR! Glorious! That was a treat to the eyes. Tossed up outside off, Powell skips down the track and creams it through covers to find the fence. He was very assured with what he was doing.
Well bowled! Slow through the air, perhaps the slider. Powell stays behind it and somehow defends it.
Hope is off the mark! Fullish delivery on middle, Shai makes room and slices his drive towards backward point where the fielder dives to his left to make a decent stop. A single taken.
Bowls it fast and flat on leg stump, Hope is circumspect in approach and blocks it to short leg.
Ends the over with a delivery down the leg side. Powell looks to glance that but misses. Dickwella gets an awkward bounce but he does well to hang on to it.
Dishes out a pitched delivery, it is on the off stump line. Powell defends it off the front foot.
Follows it up with a short ball, the southpaw ducks under it and lets it go.
Shorter in length from Kumara, the batsman moves across to flick that but misses and gets hit on the thigh pad. A stifled appeal from the bowler but the umpire ignores it.
Bangs it in short on the stumps, the batsman bends down in time and lets it through.
FOUR! Just gorgeous! Fuller length ball on the off stump line, Powell gets on the front foot and powers the drive past his partner. The ball beats the man at mid off and races away to the boundary.
Fuller length ball from Herath to end the over, the batsman pushes to mid on.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Drives to the right of the bowler and gets off strike with a quick single.
Defends it on the leg side.
Flatter ball outside off, Powell goes back to cut that one, but fails to make contact with the ball.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Ripper from Kumara! Another superb delivery, he bowls it seam up and it rises sharply. Hope goes back to defend that but the ball zips past the outside edge of the bat.
Shai Hope walks out to bat.

OUT! EDGED AND TAKEN! Second wicket down for the Windies and both the openers are back in the shed. Kumara was the man for the visitors in the first innings and he makes an impact with the ball straightaway. Bowls a short of a length ball outside off, the ball moves away after pitching and jumps a little extra than the batsman expected it to. Brathwaite stays back and loosely plays away from his body. The ball catches the outside edge. Dickwella reacts quickly, dives to his right and pouches it pretty neatly.
Drifting in from outside off, Brathwaite punches it through mid-wicket for a brace.
Angling in from outside off, the batsman defends it down the track.
Another full ball and Powell doesn't hold back. He goes hard at that one and gets an inside edge to fine leg for a single.
Bowls it full on off and the batsman smashes it to covers. The fielder there dives to his left and gets a hand to it. The Windies pair still get a couple.
Lahiru Kumara comes into the attack. He was the most successful bowler for Sri Lanka in the first innings. What can he dish out for his side in this innings?
Powell eases it in the gap on the off side for a single.
Played to mid-wicket region by the batsman.
Faster on the stumps, Brathwaite taps it with the spin to mid-wicket for a single.
Fires it full on the stumps, the batsman pushes it to mid on.
Loopy delivery on the stumps, Brathwaite defends it down the track.
Defends it to the vacant point region and they take a single.
Bowls from the edge of the crease and angles it in. Brathwaite watchfully defends it back to the bowler.
On the fourth stump channel, the batsman judges it to perfection and lets it go.
Drifting well down leg, the left-hander nudges it away to fine leg and gets off strike.
Angles it in from outside off, Powell blocks it back to the bowler.
On a good length from Lakmal and outside off. The batsman decides to let it go.
Fuller length ball on the stumps, the batsman punches it back to the bowler, who bends down quickly and makes a good stop.
Drops it short and outside off. The batsman makes room and slaps it through point. Lakmal chases the ball and pulls it inside the ropes. A couple more added to the total.
The batsman gets a massive stride forward to the pitch of it and blocks.
Floated delivery on the stumps, the batsman defends it back to Herath.
Pushes it quicker through the air, the batsman dabs it on the off side.
Slider from Herath on the stumps, Brathwaite taps it to mid-wicket.
Loopy delivery outside off  stump, the batsman lunges on the front foot and lets it go.
Bowls it fuller and attacks the stumps, Powell defends it solidly.
A widish delivery from Lakmal, the batsman doesn't play at that one.
Slipping down leg, the batsman securely works it wide of the man at leg gully. The ball rolls to fine leg and they take  a run.
Bowls it fullish and attacks the stumps. Brathwaite defends it down the track.
Much fuller from Lakmal on middle and leg. The batsman stays back and defends it on the off side.
Fuller length ball on off, the batsman drops it on the off side. They take a quick single.
Shorter in length outside off, cut away to the man at backward point.
On a flatter trajectory on off, skidding after pitching. Kraigg hangs back and blocks it out.
Well bowled! The wily old fox tosses this one up generously. Brathwaite uses his feet but is not quite to the pitch of it. Ends up jamming it out somehow.
Herath drags his length back, Kraigg camps back and cuts it towards point.
Drinks break.
Outside off, patted back towards the bowler.
Fullish on middle and leg, Powell is nimble on his feet and knocks it down to long on for a run.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
FOUR! Superb shot from Powell to open his account. Short of a length ball outside off, the batsman stands tall and powers it through the covers for a boundary.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Kieran Powell is the next man in.

OUT! Chopped on! Lakmal finally gets his man. So two in two for Lakmal but the scoreboard will show just one wicket against his name and he has only himself to blame for that. He bowled Smith off the previous ball but he had overstepped, so this time he looks at the umpire first and then starts his celebration. Sri Lanka have got the opening they wanted, can they nip out a few more and make a comeback of sorts? Coming to the delivery - It is pitched on a fuller length by Lakmal and well outside off, seeing the width, Smith decides to play the expansive drive. He doesn't move his feet and tries to reach that one. He ends up getting a thick inside edge which goes on to hit the stumps. After getting a start, the southpaw fails to make a substantial contribution.

FIVE NO BALLS! BOWLED, BUT OFF A NO BALL! Oh boy, the rub of the green isn't going Sri Lanka's way! A length ball from Lakmal, slanting in sharply and seams a little. Smith is caught in the crease as he looks to play that. The ball sneaks through his defenses and hits the timber. Lakmal starts to celebrate but turns around to see that the umpire has his hand outstretched. He has overstepped and is heartbroken. The ball races away to the boundary as the fielders were busy celebrating, so five runs added to the total.
The leg slip moves to the short leg position, but the bowler goes for the double bluff. Decides to bowl it wide outside off. The batsman waits back and chops it to deep point for a brace.
Starts with a delivery on the leg stump line. Smith goes back to flick that length ball but misses it and gets hit on the pads.
Darts it on middle and leg stump line, the batsman defends it back to the bowler.
The batsman charges down the wicket and dead-bats it.

Turn and bounce! Herath and rest of the spinners will be licking their lips seeing that. The ball lands on a length outside off and grips off the surface, the batsman decides to defend that but he is beaten for the away turn.
Loopy ball, the batsman steps out and punches it to long on for a single.
Attacks the stumps and the batsman taps it on the leg side.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Time for some spin, the wily veteran, Rangana Herath, comes into the attack. Can he spin a web over the Windies batters?
In the channel outside off, Kraigg decides to leave that one.
Brathwaite comes on the front foot and defends it on the off side.
Change of angle for Lakmal, decides to go around the wicket and attacks the pads with a full delivery. Smith fails to put bat to ball. The ball goes off his pads to mid-wicket. They take a leg bye.
Width on offer and the batsman slaps it hard to point. Though can't find the gap.
FOUR! Wow, a brilliant reply from Smith, he gets an overpitched delivery from Lakmal. The left-hander leans forward and creams it past his partner. The ball races to the long off fence.

LOUD SHOUT FOR AN LBW! Fuller length ball on middle and leg, it keeps a touch low, Smith hangs back to flick that but misses and gets pinged on the pads. Appeal from the Sri Lankan fielders but the umpire shakes his head. Dickwella did indicate that it might be pitching outside leg and they decide not to take the referral.
Length ball outside off, the batsman doesn't play at it.
Again too straight from Gamage, the batsman uses his wrists and flicks it past the short leg fielder for a brace.

FOUR! With that boundary, the Windies lead by 250! Length ball on the leg stump line, Brathwaite plays a delicate leg glance and beats the keeper with it. The ball races away to the fine leg boundary.
Once again, the bowler decides to keep it full. The batsman defends it solidly.
Fuller in length and outside off, Brathwaite leans forward and drills it to mid off. Can't find the gap.
Low full toss on the stumps, the batsman punches it to mid on. The fielder dives to his left and makes a good stop.
Shorter in length, coming in from outside off. Smith decides to play the pull but misses and gets hit on the thigh pad.
Spraying on the pads and the batsman works it to deep square leg for a single.
Touch too straight, the batsman tucks it on the leg side for a single.

Bowls from around the wicket, slanting in from outside off. Smith hangs back to flick that but gets hit on the pads. There is an elongated appeal for an LBW but the umpire is unmoved. After a chat with his bowler and the keeper, Chandimal decides not to go for the referral. It looked a little high and might have missed the leg stump as well.
FOUR! Pulled with authority! He looks in great rhythm, sees the shortish delivery early and gets into position quickly. Pulls it powerfully through square leg for a boundary.
Wrong line from Lakmal, bowls it fuller on the leg stump line. Smith looks to glance that but misses.
Tailing in from outside off, the batsman aims to play the drive but gets it off the inner half on the leg side.
A harmless delivery from Gamange, full and outside off. The batsman lets it through to the keeper.
Dipping in sharply from outside off, Kraigg stays back and nudges it to mid-wicket.
Serves up a good length ball outside off, the batsman chooses to leave.
Fullish delivery, swings in a little, the batsman taps it on the leg side.
Short of a length ball from Gamage, the batsman punches it to mid off. They take a quick single.
Innocuous delivery outside off, Brathwaite doesn't play at it.
Lakmal tries the short ball, hits the deck half way through. The batsman bends down quickly and lets it through.
Away swinging delivery from Lakmal on a length outside off. Brathwaite decides to let it be.
Punches it off the back foot to the man at extra cover.
Good length ball outside off, the batsman lets it through to the keeper.
Bowls it fuller on the stumps and the batsman sits back in his crease as he defends it down the track.
Shortish delivery from Gamage, the batsman slaps it but finds the man at backward point.
Fuller in length and angling away from the stumps. No shot offered by the batsman.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Wide delivery and it swings further away from the batsman. Smith doesn't play at it.
Spears in a fullish delivery on the stumps, Smith jams his bat down in time and digs it out.
Moving away just a little and seeing that, Smith decides to let it be.
Shortish delivery on the stumps, Braithwaite goes back and defends it.
Bouncer from Lakmal, the batsman ducks under it and lets it go.
Shortish delivery down leg, the left-hander goes across to pull that but gets a glove to it. The ball rolls to fine leg for a single.
Plays away from the body and pushes it in the gap on the off side for a single.
Sharp nut from Lakmal, superb delivery! Shortish in length and it moves away at pace. The batsman does well to take his hands away from the line of it.
Lakmal bowls it fuller and this one too keeps a little low. Brathwaite pushes it on the off side.
Fuller length ball, angling across, the batsman covers his stumps and lets it go.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Played through mid-wicket by the batsman.

This is interesting from Devon, he goes after the short ball and makes his intentions clear. He will go after anything that is in his zone. Short and outside off. Goes for the pull but top edges it over the slip cordon. Mathews can't get there in time and the batsmen take two.
Short of a length ball outside off, the batsman defends it on the off side.

FOUR! SHOT! Devon Smith is off the mark with a positive strike. He got run out in a poor manner in the first innings but this shot will give him a lot of confidence. Short and wide outside off. The left-hander slaps it through the covers.
Lahiru Gamage will share the attack with Suranga Lakmal.
Short of a length ball, this one rises normally and the batsman decides to let it be.
THIS IS INTERESTING! Another one keeps low and it is in line with the stumps. Brathwaite keeps his eyes on it and just manages to defend it.
Attacks the stumps with a delivery on a fuller length. The batsman defends it.
Fuller length ball, angling in from outside off, the batsman defends it down the track.
Lovely shape! On a good length closer to the off stump, it moves away quite nicely. Brathwaite leaves it all alone.
THAT ONE KEPT PRETTY LOW! Fuller length ball on the leg stump line, keeps low, the batsman does well to get his bat down in time and flicks it through square leg. A couple to start the proceedings.
